title: Practice Exam: Chemical Reactions and Stoichiometry
description: 15-question practice exam covering balancing equations, stoichiometry, mole concept, limiting reagents, and reaction energy.

questions.question: What is the balanced equation for: Fe + O₂ → Fe₂O₃?
questions.explanation: Balancing: Fe atoms: left 4, right 4; O atoms: left 6, right 6. The balanced equation is 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃.

questions.question: In the reaction 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, how many moles of H₂O are produced from 3 moles of H₂?
questions.explanation: Mole ratio: 2 H₂ : 2 H₂O = 1:1. Therefore, 3 mol H₂ × (2 mol H₂O / 2 mol H₂) = 3 mol H₂O.

questions.question: What is the molar mass of NaCl? (Na = 23 g/mol, Cl = 35.5 g/mol)
How many moles are in 45 g of H₂O? (Molar mass = 18 g/mol)
questions.explanation: Moles = mass / molar mass = 45 g / 18 g/mol = 2.5 mol

questions.question: Which is a decomposition reaction?
questions.explanation: Option B is decomposition: one compound (H₂O₂) breaks into two products (H₂O and O₂). A is synthesis, C is single displacement, D is combustion.

questions.question: In the reaction CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O, how many grams of CO₂ (molar mass = 44 g/mol) are produced from 8 g of CH₄ (molar mass = 16 g/mol)?
questions.explanation: Moles of CH₄ = 8/16 = 0.5 mol. Mole ratio 1:1, so 0.5 mol CO₂. Mass of CO₂ = 0.5 × 44 = 22 g.

questions.question: Which reaction is exothermic?
questions.explanation: Combustion releases heat (exothermic). Melting, evaporating, and dissolving ammonium nitrate are endothermic (absorb heat).

questions.question: A catalyst changes which of the following?
options: The equilibrium position of the reaction
The activation energy of the reaction
The amount of product formed at equilibrium
questions.explanation: A catalyst lowers activation energy without changing ΔH, equilibrium position, or the amount of product at equilibrium.

questions.question: True or False: When balancing an equation, you can change the subscripts in chemical formulas.
questions.explanation: False. Only coefficients (numbers before formulas) are adjusted. Subscripts (numbers within formulas) are never changed because that would change the identity of the compounds.

questions.question: True or False: In a combustion reaction, the products always include CO₂ and H₂O.
questions.explanation: True. In complete combustion of a hydrocarbon fuel, carbon forms CO₂ and hydrogen forms H₂O. Incomplete combustion can produce CO or soot.

questions.question: True or False: Avogadro's number is approximately 6.022 × 10²³.
questions.explanation: True. Avogadro's number is exactly 6.02214076 × 10²³, commonly rounded to 6.022 × 10²³.

questions.question: How many moles of O₂ are in 96 g of O₂? (Molar mass = 32 g/mol) _____ mol
questions.explanation: Moles = mass / molar mass = 96 g / 32 g/mol = 3 mol

questions.question: What is the molar mass of Ca(OH)₂? (Ca = 40, O = 16, H = 1) _____ g/mol
Balance the equation: Al + Cl₂ → AlCl₃. Write your answer in the form: ___Al + ___Cl₂ → ___AlCl₃
questions.explanation: Balancing: Al: 2 on each side. Cl: 6 on each side. Balanced equation: 2Al + 3Cl₂ → 2AlCl₃

questions.question: In the reaction 2N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, if you have 14 g of N₂ (molar mass = 28 g/mol) and 6 g of H₂ (molar mass = 2 g/mol), identify which is the limiting reagent and explain why.
acceptableAnswers: N₂ is the limiting reagent. With 0.5 mol N₂, we need 0.75 mol H₂, but we only have 3 mol H₂. Wait, 6/2 = 3 mol H₂. So actually, N₂ needs 0.5 mol × (3/2) = 0.75 mol H₂. We have 3 mol, which is more than enough. So N₂ is limiting? Let me recalculate: 14/28 = 0.5 mol N₂; 6/2 = 3 mol H₂. For 0.5 mol N₂, we need (3/2) × 0.5 = 0.75 mol H₂. We have 3 mol H₂, so H₂ is in excess and N₂ is limiting.
H₂ is the limiting reagent. The mole ratio requires 3 H₂ for every 2 N₂. For the given amounts, there is insufficient H₂ to react with all the N₂.
questions.explanation: Moles: N₂ = 0.5 mol, H₂ = 3 mol. For 0.5 mol N₂, we need 0.75 mol H₂ (using 2:3 ratio). Since we have 3 mol H₂ (more than enough), N₂ is the limiting reagent.
